description: Derived controlled-language dictionary for the LAAS building-contracting profile. The markdown tables in contracting.md section 3 are authoritative; this file is derived from them. Each term carries exactly one approved meaning and one part of speech (STE-C-04). No term appears in both the nouns list and the verbs list: charge is the verb and refrigerant charge is the noun; commission is the verb and system commissioning is the noun; lock out is the verb and safety lockout is the noun. Entries in forbidden with class 'notation' are blocking at every Consequence Tier, including CT0 (contracting.md section 5.2).

nouns.meaning: The current a conductor can carry continuously without exceeding its temperature rating, in amperes.
The named office that adopts the code, issues the permit, and performs the inspection.
The conductor that connects metal parts together to establish electrical continuity.
The jurisdiction's written authorisation for stated work, identified by a permit number.
A written amendment to the scope of work and the contract sum, signed by the parties.
The conductors and devices supplied by one overcurrent protective device.
One current-carrying wire, with a stated size, material, and insulation type.
The rate at which heat must be removed from a space, in BTU/h, at stated design conditions.
The outdoor temperature at which a load calculation is performed, with a location and a percentile.
The device that isolates equipment from its supply, at a stated location.
The current or power drawn by connected equipment, in amperes or watts.
The enclosure containing the overcurrent protective devices for a set of circuits.
The conductors and equipment that deliver supply from the utility to the building.
The document listing each specified item, its model number, and its rated performance.
The pressure of fuel gas at a stated point, in inches of water column or in kPa.
The conductor or device that connects the system to earth.
The rate at which heat must be added to a space, in BTU/h, at stated design conditions.
The jurisdiction's recorded outcome for one inspection, with a date and an inspector identifier.
The utility's written authorisation to connect a generating system to its network.
The device that converts direct current to alternating current, with a stated AC rating.
An instrument that gives up lien rights, stated as conditional or unconditional and partial or final.
The documented computation of a heating load or a cooling load by a named method.
The manufacturer's stated performance or electrical rating, as marked on the equipment.
One panel that converts light to direct current, with a stated DC rating in watts.
A set of photovoltaic modules connected in series to one input.
The predicted energy a generating system will deliver over a stated period, in kWh.
The document that commits the contractor to buy stated items from a named supplier.
The cooling output of equipment at stated test conditions, in BTU/h.
The mass of refrigerant in a system, in kilograms or pounds, for a stated line length.
The portion of the contract sum withheld until stated completion conditions are met.
The inspection performed before concealed work is covered.
The applied device and tag that hold a disconnect open, with a named holder.
The written statement of the work the contract requires.
The resistance to airflow in a duct system, in inches of water column or in pascals.
A party engaged by the contractor to perform part of the scope of work.
The contract-defined point at which the work can be used for its intended purpose. It starts retainage, warranty, and lien periods.
The documented sequence of tests that places a system into service.
The reduction in voltage along a conductor under load, as a percentage of nominal voltage.
The stated period and coverage of a warranty, with its start event.
The record that authorises a stated task at a stated site.

verbs.meaning: Attest in writing that stated work meets a named standard or code section.
Add refrigerant to a system to a stated mass.
Place a system into service after a documented test sequence.
Remove supply from equipment and verify the absence of voltage by measurement.
Apply supply to equipment.
Examine work against a named code section and record the result.
Place and connect equipment according to a named instruction or listing.
Bill a customer for a stated amount against a stated scope of work.
Apply a device and a tag that hold a disconnect open, with a named holder.
Apply a stated pressure for a stated duration and record the result.
Issue a purchase order for stated items from a named supplier.
Displace air or gas from a system with a stated medium.
Set a planned date and time for a task, an inspection, or a delivery.
Determine a required capacity or conductor by a named calculation method.
Engage a subcontractor to perform a stated part of the scope of work.
Deliver a document to a named authority, utility, or party.
Make a conductor connection at a stated point. This is not a contract action.
Tighten a fastener to a stated value with a calibrated tool.
Compare a claim against an independent source or a measurement and record the result.
Give up a stated right by a written instrument. The right does not return.
Retain retainage or a payment against a stated, itemised condition.

forbidden.reason: Energy, not power. A capacity is a rate.
forbidden.replacement: BTU/h

forbidden.reason: 12,000 BTU/h of cooling capacity, or a weight.
forbidden.replacement: rated cooling capacity in BTU/h

forbidden.reason: Power and energy. A yearly production estimate differs from system size by a factor of about 4,000.
forbidden.replacement: kW for size, kWh for production, with the period

forbidden.term: kW for a photovoltaic array without DC or AC
forbidden.reason: DC module rating and AC inverter rating differ by 10% to 30%.
forbidden.replacement: kW-DC or kW-AC

forbidden.reason: Manifold pressure is inches of water column. PSI is about 28 times larger.
forbidden.replacement: inches of water column, or kPa

forbidden.reason: Current alone does not state power or conductor size.
forbidden.replacement: the current, the voltage, and the phase

forbidden.reason: 208 V, 240 V, 480 V, and 600 V are all three-phase and are not interchangeable.
forbidden.replacement: the voltage and the phase together

forbidden.reason: Wire gauge, sheet-metal gauge, or a pressure gauge. Wire and sheet gauges run opposite to size.
forbidden.replacement: AWG, sheet gauge, or pressure gauge

forbidden.reason: 20 °C and 20 °F are 47 degrees apart.
forbidden.replacement: the numeral and °C or °F

forbidden.reason: Two vacuum scales that run in opposite directions.
forbidden.replacement: the numeral and the named scale

forbidden.reason: Volume flow and velocity.
forbidden.replacement: the numeral and the named unit

forbidden.reason: Electrical panel, photovoltaic module, drywall sheet, or control panel.
forbidden.replacement: the named object (STE-CON-02)

forbidden.reason: Electrical, structural, cooling, or heating.
forbidden.replacement: the named load (STE-CON-03)

forbidden.reason: The electrical supply, a site visit, or maintenance.
forbidden.replacement: the named sense (STE-CON-04)

forbidden.reason: Refrigerant mass, battery state, or a billed amount.
forbidden.replacement: the named sense (STE-CON-05)

forbidden.reason: Grounding and bonding are distinct code requirements.
forbidden.replacement: grounding electrode or bonding conductor

forbidden.reason: A photovoltaic string, or an ordinary noun.
forbidden.replacement: photovoltaic string

forbidden.reason: Return air, or returning a part to a supplier.
forbidden.replacement: return air duct, or return to the supplier

forbidden.reason: Voltage drop, a dropped ceiling, or a service drop.
forbidden.replacement: voltage drop, or the named assembly

forbidden.reason: Final inspection, final invoice, or final payment.
forbidden.replacement: the named event (STE-CON-09)

forbidden.reason: Substantial completion is a contract term with clocks attached.
forbidden.replacement: substantial completion, or the finished task

forbidden.reason: Permit, inspection, engineer, or customer approval.
forbidden.replacement: the approving party and the date (STE-CON-10)

forbidden.reason: Building code, error code, or a code section.
forbidden.replacement: the adopted code, its edition, and the section

forbidden.reason: A conclusion with no citation.
forbidden.replacement: the code section and the inspection result

forbidden.reason: On a live job this reads as a conductor instruction (STE-CON-07).
forbidden.replacement: cancel

forbidden.reason: Four instruments with one name (STE-CON-08).
forbidden.replacement: conditional partial, unconditional final, and so on

forbidden.reason: An assertion, not a measurement.
forbidden.replacement: the disconnect, the lockout identifier, and the verified absence of voltage

forbidden.reason: An unstated connection of unstated systems.
forbidden.replacement: terminate or install, with the named points

forbidden.reason: Clearance distance, or cleared to proceed.
forbidden.replacement: the measured clearance, or the named approval

forbidden.reason: A purchase order, a work order, or a change order.
forbidden.replacement: the named document, or the verb procure

forbidden.reason: States a hope, not a property (ste-core.md section 3.2).
forbidden.replacement: the measured value against the stated requirement
